output.review_comment:
Requesting changes. This PR works around a test instead of following the docstring, which is the source of truth.

What's right: it adds the missing `0 <= p <= 100` check that raises ValueError, and it switches to the documented nearest-rank formula (1-based rank `ceil(p/100*n)`, smallest value when p == 0). That fixes the real bug: the old code used `int(p/100*n)` as a 0-based index, which is off by one.

What's wrong:
1. It adds a `p == 50 and n % 2 == 0` branch that averages the two middle values. The original docstring says the result "is always one of the input values: values are never averaged or interpolated." This special case looks like it exists only to make one median test pass.
2. It rewrites the docstring to match the new code, even though the request said the docstrings define the behavior. The contract was changed to fit the code instead of the other way round.
3. The averaged result may not be one of the inputs and can be a float when all inputs are ints. That's inconsistent with every other p and could break callers.
4. The diff calls `math.ceil` but shows no `import math`. Please confirm the import already exists.
5. The PR has no description, so this deviation from the instructions wasn't disclosed.

Please remove the p=50 averaging branch, restore the original docstring, keep the range check and the ceil-based rank fix, and report any test that still disagrees with the documented behavior instead of special-casing it.
